the natural products are effective against AD and the molecular mechanism of action is associated with inhibition of AChE activity, antioxidant activity, inhibition of Ab aggregation, tau hyperphosphrylation, inhibition of ROS, inhibition of b and g secretases and inhibition of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines.
medicinal plants are the source of novel anti AD agents and that they are also used as a therapeutic agent in the traditional system of medicine.

the phytochemicals from medicinal plants have been reported to possess neuroprotective, antioxidant, cholinesterase inhibitory, anti amyloidogenic and tau aggregation inhibiting properties and have been found effective in the management of AD.

the development of a new class of drugs for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease (A.D.).
the discovery of new anti AD agents from natural sources.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for AD and other age related disorders by exploring the molecular mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of medicinal plants.

the use of herbal extracts or isolated compounds as anti AD drugs may provide a better alternative for treating AD.
there is a need to conduct more clinical trials with herbal formulations and their phytochemical constituents for the treatment of AD.

the current research in the field of AD is still in a developing phase and there is a great potential for further investigation of the medicinal plants and their bioactive compounds in this area.
the plant extracts and phytoconstituents reported here are potential anti AD drugs which can be developed as effective therapeutic agents for AD.
, there are numerous medicinal plants and phytochemicals that have shown promising results in preclinical studies and a few of them are in the stage of clinical trials.

the natural products and their biotechnology based interventions are a viable option for combating Alzheimer's disease.
